# Ricardo Orellana — Senior Software Engineer

- **Location:** Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico
- **Current role:** Senior Software Engineer at Change.org (since October 2025)
- **Experience:** Building since 2015, across 6 engineering teams
- **Focus:** Web, mobile, and full-stack development
- **Website:** https://ricardoorellana.github.io/

## Summary

I’m Ricardo, a software engineer in Guadalajara, Mexico. I turn complex problems into software that feels simple. Since 2015, I’ve built mobile apps, trading platforms, and the systems behind them. These days, I’m a Senior Software Engineer at Change.org. I like understanding the problem, working closely with people, and leaving the code a little easier to work with.

## Experience

### Senior Software Engineer — Change.org
**2025-10 – Present**

I’m working on tools that help people speak up about the things they care about. At Change.org, that means helping turn a personal concern into a petition, a conversation, and a chance to make something happen.

### Senior Software Engineer — ARCOS LLC
**2024-11 – 2025-09**

I worked across the frontend and backend of the ARCOS platform. A lot of the job was connecting the pieces: building features, keeping the application responsive, and making sure it could grow without getting harder to use.

### Software Engineer — Bitso
**2021 – 2024**

I helped bring new features from an idea to a release, working with product, design, mobile, and backend teams. Along the way, I helped shape the tech stack and mentored React developers, sharing patterns that made everyday work easier.

### Senior Software Engineer — EPAM Systems Mexico
**2018 – 2021**

I built and maintained software across client projects, with a focus on code other engineers could understand and test. I also planned delivery, documented technical decisions, and helped teammates work through tricky implementation details.

### Lead Software Engineer — Rever Inc.
**2017 – 2018**

I led development across the frontend and backend, and introduced microservices as the platform grew. I also looked after development, staging, and production, adding automation, monitoring, and logging so we could see what was happening and keep things running.

### Front-End / Mobile Developer — Propelics
**2015 – 2017**

This is where I got my start: building apps for iOS, Android, and mobile web with JavaScript and Appcelerator Titanium. Moving between platforms taught me to follow a bug carefully, pay attention to performance, and think about the person on the other side of the screen.

## Selected work

These are team projects I contributed to. Dates follow the project timeline and may differ from employment dates. The illustrations on the site are original interpretations, not product screenshots.

### Bitso Exchanger (2020)

I contributed to a cryptocurrency exchange that helps people buy and sell digital assets. The goal: make a complicated financial product feel straightforward to use.

### Power E*TRADE (2018)

A trading platform that brings stocks, options, and futures together. I contributed to a product where a clear interface matters when there’s a lot to keep track of.

### Continuous Improvement (2017)

A web and mobile app that gives manufacturing employees a place to share ideas and improve the way they work. Practical tools for the people closest to the problem.

### Apple Financial Services (2016)

A mobile app for putting together quotes for Apple products. It brought an enterprise workflow onto a smaller screen, where clarity and ease of use matter even more.

### Audithere (2015)

A mobile app for auditing items. One of my early projects, and a chance to turn a hands-on process into something people could carry in their pocket.
